findings.summary: Page 1 shows the response flow as a fragmented list of node labels, so the Promise-then-body-stream sequence is hard to follow.
findings.evidence:
fetch(url, options)
call
Promise<Response>
resolves on headers
Body stream
read later
findings.fix: Render it as a clear left-to-right diagram: fetch() → Promise<Response> (resolves on headers) → body stream (read later via res.json()/text()).

findings.summary: A single bullet packs seven options into one line, and the page gives no explanation of what each one does.
findings.evidence: Options: method (default GET), headers, body, credentials, mode, cache, signal
findings.fix: Turn the options into a two-column table (option | purpose) or split them into one-line bullets.

findings.summary: Page 2 has bullets that hold two ideas, and the clone advice is separate from the 'read once' rule it belongs to.
findings.evidence: fetch rejects only on network failure or abort / HTTP 404/500 still resolve; Body is read once; bodyUsed becomes true
findings.fix: Split into one idea per bullet: 'Rejects: network failure, abort' and 'HTTP 404/500 still resolve'; 'Body is read once' and 'bodyUsed becomes true'.

findings.summary: The code is shown with a catch-and-ignore pattern and the 'ignore the abort names' bullet is vague, and the TimeoutError name is introduced before the timeout section explains it.
findings.evidence: Ignore the abort names; rethrow real errors ... e.name === 'AbortError' || e.name === 'TimeoutError'
findings.fix: Say 'Ignore AbortError (cancel) and TimeoutError (timeout); rethrow everything else' and move the TimeoutError check to the timeout section.

findings.summary: Cookie scope is given as 'Origin + Path', but cookies are scoped by domain (host) and path, not by origin.
findings.evidence: Scope | All tabs, one origin | That tab only | Origin + Path
findings.fix: Write 'Domain + Path' for cookies. Add that cookies ignore port, and that the Secure and SameSite attributes control scheme and cross-site sending.

findings.summary: The cookie scope row says cookies are scoped to 'Origin + Path', but cookies are scoped by domain and path, not origin.
findings.evidence: Scope | All tabs, one origin | That tab only | Origin + Path
findings.fix: Change the cookie cell to 'Domain + Path'. Add that cookies ignore port and, by default, scheme, unlike web storage, which is per origin.

findings.summary: XSS is used as the reason for keeping secrets out of web storage but is never defined.
findings.evidence: Any XSS script can read localStorage and sessionStorage. Tokens go in an HttpOnly cookie.
findings.fix: Gloss it on first use, for example: 'XSS (cross-site scripting: attacker-injected JavaScript running on your page)'.

findings.summary: Page 4 repeats facts in two sections and several bullets hold more than one idea.
findings.evidence: Size | ~5MB | ~5MB | ~4KB ... Synchronous, ~5MB per origin, values are strings only; HttpOnly cookie is unreadable by JS, so keep auth tokens there / No secrets in web storage
findings.fix: Drop the repeated size line from the API section; split 'synchronous', 'strings only' and 'getItem returns null' into separate bullets.

findings.summary: The page says onupgradeneeded runs only after a bumped version, but it also runs when the database is first created.
findings.evidence:
Schema changes only in onupgradeneeded
It runs only after a bumped version
findings.fix: Write 'It runs when the database is first created or when open() is given a higher version than the stored one'.

findings.summary: The 'URLSearchParams' section mixes unrelated facts and the encoding functions table, and the page ends with a bullet that holds two ideas.
findings.evidence: Space becomes + here, but %20 in encodeURIComponent / fetch(url) takes a URL object; URLSearchParams works as body
findings.fix: Split into separate bullets, and move the encodeURI vs encodeURIComponent table under its own heading.
